question.:question/problem:
Differentiate $2f(t)+3g(t)$ with respect to $t$, where

 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =\left(2 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,i\right)+\left(- 9 \cos{\left(t \right)}\,j+3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\,k\right) \\ g(t) & =\left((5 - \sin{\left(t \right)})\,i\right)+\left(3\,j\right)+\left(- 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\,k\right)\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the constant multiple and the sum rules, we have 

$$
(2f(t)+3g(t))^{′}=2{f}^{′}(t)+3{g}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's find the derivatives of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2 \sin{\left(t \right)})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 9 \cos{\left(t \right)})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 \cos{\left(t \right)})\,k \\  & =\left(2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\,i\right)+\left(9 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,j\right)+\left(- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,k\right) \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5 - \sin{\left(t \right)})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 2 \cos{\left(t \right)})\,k \\  & =\left(- \cos{\left(t \right)}\,i\right)+\left(2 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,k\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Hence 

$$
\begin{aligned}(2f(t)+3g(t))^{′} & =2{f}^{′}(t)+3{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =2\left(\left(2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\,i\right)+\left(9 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,j\right)+\left(- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,k\right)\right)+3\left(\left(- \cos{\left(t \right)}\,i\right)+\left(2 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,k\right)\right) \\  & =\left(4 \cos{\left(t \right)}\,i\right)+\left(18 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,j\right)+\left(- 6 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,k\right)+\left(- 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\,i\right)+\left(6 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,k\right) \\  & =\left(\cos{\left(t \right)}\,i\right)+\left(18 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,j\right)\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}g(t) & =⟨2 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,9 - 9 t,\,t^{2}⟩ \\ h(t) & =⟨2 \sin{\left(t \right)},\,3 t,\,-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the constant multiple and the sum rules, we have

$$
(2g(t)-h(t))^{′}=2{g}^{′}(t)-{h}^{′}(t)
$$

Let's now find the derivatives of each function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2 \cos{\left(t \right)}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(9 - 9 t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)},\,-9,\,2 t⟩ \\ {h}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2 \sin{\left(t \right)}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-4)⟩ \\  & =⟨2 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,3,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(2g(t)-h(t))^{′} & =2{g}^{′}(t)-{h}^{′}(t) \\  & =2⟨- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)},\,-9,\,2 t⟩-⟨2 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,3,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨- 4 \sin{\left(t \right)},\,-18,\,4 t⟩-⟨2 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,3,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨- 4 \sin{\left(t \right)} - 2 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,-21,\,4 t⟩ \\  & =⟨- 4 \sin{\left(t \right)} - 2 \cos{\left(t \right)},\,-21,\,4 t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

By the sum rule, we have

$$
(f(t)+g(t))^{′}={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t)
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 - 9 t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 t - 18),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 7 t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-9,\,3,\,-7⟩ \\ {g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 3 t^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 t^{2} - 3),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- t)⟩ \\  & =⟨- 6 t,\,6 t,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}(f(t)+g(t))^{′} & ={f}^{′}(t)+{g}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨-9,\,3,\,-7⟩+⟨- 6 t,\,6 t,\,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨- 6 t - 9,\,6 t + 3,\,-8⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$
(f(t)+4g(t))^{′}={f}^{′}(t)+4{g}^{′}(t).

$$

$$
